article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: Blueberry × 707 Headband
Breeder: Humboldt Seed Organization
THC Content: 19–23%
CBD Content: 0.1%
Terpene Profile: pinene , terpinolene, myrcene
Primary Flavors: Blueberry, sweet fruit, spice, anise, pine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 65–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Mid-October
Indoor Yield: 450–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 1,000–4,000 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Blueberry Headband approaches the familiar fruit-and-fuel combination from a distinctly Humboldt perspective. Beneath its sweet berry surface sits a vigorous California hybrid capable of producing enormous outdoor plants, dense resinous flowers, and a much heavier finish than the name alone might suggest. Humboldt Seed Organization developed the cultivar around Blueberry genetics and its own Headband material, creating a weed that begins with a lively cerebral lift before gradually settling into a deeper physical state. The breeder currently identifies the plant as 70% indica and 30% sativa, with THC between 19% and 23%, a 65-to-70-day indoor flowering cycle, and the potential for exceptionally large outdoor harvests.
Genetics and Lineage

Humboldt Seed Organization currently lists Blueberry Headband as Blueberry × 707 Headband. There is an interesting historical wrinkle, however. In a 2014 breeder article discussing the strain’s development, HSO stated that the original project began with DJ Short ‘s original Blueberry crossed to an F3 Emerald Headband male. The company subsequently continued working the population for greater yield, resistance, flavor, and stability, eventually describing the reworked version as F6. These two official descriptions are best viewed as different stages or naming conventions within the breeding program rather than evidence that Blueberry Headband is simply an unidentified Blueberry-and-Headband cross.

The Blueberry half supplies much of the cultivar’s recognizable fruit character and contributes to its tendency toward colorful flowers. DJ Short’s Blueberry lineage is also associated with broad-leaf structure, rich resin production, and a mellow physical dimension. Headband moves the profile in another direction, adding vigor, potency, spice, fuel, and a more animated cerebral component. When those traits combine successfully, the result feels less like a dessert strain and more like ripe berry sweetness layered over pungent, resinous California marijuana.

Breeding work after the original cross appears to have been significant. HSO specifically described selecting for increased production, stronger resistance, and improved flavor while moving the line through additional generations. That helps explain why the cultivar can display both vigorous vertical growth and unusually heavy flower production despite its predominantly indica classification.
Effects and Experience

The first stage of the experience tends to arrive in the mind rather than the limbs. A noticeable rise in mood can develop alongside greater engagement with conversation, music, creative work, or whatever happens to be occupying attention. The cerebral portion is energetic enough to prevent this cannabis strain from feeling immediately sleepy, yet it normally carries more composure than the sharper rush associated with many sativa-dominant varieties. Humboldt’s own description emphasizes a combination of cerebral and physical effects with substantial potency and duration.

Physical relaxation becomes more noticeable as the high develops. Shoulders loosen, tension begins to recede, and the initially active mental state settles into something warmer and less demanding. That progression is one of the cultivar’s defining qualities: it can feel upbeat during the opening portion without remaining relentlessly stimulating for the entire session. HSO’s earlier breeding notes similarly characterized the experience as uplifting and active before ending in a relaxing body high.

At 19–23% THC according to the breeder, this is not especially forgiving marijuana for someone with little tolerance. Large doses can shift the pleasant heaviness toward sleepiness, mental fog, or THC-related discomfort. Moderate use generally preserves more of the berry hybrid’s distinctive transition from bright mental lift to full-body ease.
Medical Benefits

Blueberry Headband’s combination of mood elevation and muscular relaxation helps explain its popularity among medical cannabis consumers seeking a middle ground between an energizing daytime variety and a strongly sedating nighttime weed. Some people gravitate toward this type of balanced effect when dealing with temporary stress, persistent physical discomfort, tension, low mood, or difficulty relaxing after an active day.

Its relatively high THC concentration may contribute to the perception of substantial pain relief, but cultivar-specific medical evidence is limited. Blueberry Headband itself has not been established through controlled clinical trials as a treatment for chronic pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, migraine, or another medical disorder. The therapeutic effects of cannabis also depend on dose, individual physiology, cannabinoid content, terpene composition, and tolerance rather than the strain name alone.

Patients who respond poorly to high-THC marijuana should use particular caution. An initially pleasant cerebral lift can become overly intense with excessive consumption, and very large doses may produce dizziness, anxiety, or impaired concentration. For medical use, knowing the cannabinoid analysis of the actual flower is more informative than relying exclusively on the cultivar’s reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fruit is unmistakable, but Blueberry Headband has considerably more going on than straightforward blueberry sweetness. Breaking apart a mature flower can release dark berry, sweet vegetation, pine, and spice before a sharper resinous note appears underneath. Humboldt Seed Organization specifically highlights fruity aromas accompanied by spice and anise, an unusual combination that gives the cultivar a more complex finish than many berry-dominant hybrids.

Inhaled, the sweeter Blueberry side generally arrives first. Ripe berries and soft fruit give way to peppery spice, pine, herbal anise, and an earthy or lightly fuel-like finish from the Headband ancestry. Cooler-grown flowers can also develop striking red and purple coloration, providing a visual counterpart to the dark-fruit aroma. HSO notes that lower nighttime temperatures during flowering can encourage those reddish and purplish tones.

There is no single terpene formula that applies to every Blueberry Headband flower. Commercial laboratory data attached to the strain name show considerable variation, which is expected with different growers and phenotypes. Pinene, terpinolene, myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene all appear in contemporary profiles, but a certificate of analysis from the actual harvest remains the best way to determine dominant terpenes.
Growing Information

Blueberry Headband can become much larger than its indica-dominant classification might lead a grower to expect. Humboldt describes vigorous growth and specifically warns indoor cultivators to control its height. The breeder lists outdoor plants around three meters tall, while an earlier HSO catalog described exceptional specimens reaching three to four meters under favorable conditions. Strong lateral branches and substantial stretch make early canopy management valuable indoors.

Topping, low-stress training, and screen-of-green methods are practical ways to convert that vigor into productive flowering area. The indoor bloom period is approximately 65–70 days, with expected yields around 450–600 g/m². Flowers typically become dense and heavily resinous as maturity approaches, and good air exchange around the canopy is worthwhile whenever large colas develop.

Outdoor cultivation reveals the plant’s commercial-scale potential. HSO gives a mid-October harvest and an extraordinary yield range of approximately one to four kilograms per plant when conditions permit. Those numbers assume substantial root space, abundant sunlight, a long vegetative season, appropriate nutrition, and a climate capable of supporting large plants into autumn. In smaller containers or less favorable environments, actual harvests will naturally be much lower.
FAQ
Is Blueberry Headband an indica or sativa?

Humboldt Seed Organization classifies its version as approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa. Despite the indica dominance, the plant can grow vigorously and produce a noticeable cerebral component before its heavier physical effects develop.
What are the genetics of Blueberry Headband?

The breeder’s current specification is Blueberry × 707 Headband. An older official HSO account describes the original breeding project more specifically as DJ Short’s Blueberry crossed with an F3 Emerald Headband male, followed by additional selection through later generations.
How much THC does Blueberry Headband have?
Humboldt Seed Organization lists THC between approximately 19% and 23% and CBD around 0.1%. Individual harvests can fall outside those figures depending on phenotype and cultivation conditions.
What does Blueberry Headband taste like?

Sweet blueberry and ripe fruit form the core flavor, followed by spice, pine, herbs, anise, earth, and occasional fuel-like undertones. The combination is richer and more pungent than a simple fruit-flavored strain.
How long does Blueberry Headband take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 65–70 days according to Humboldt Seed Organization. Outdoor plants generally reach harvest around the middle of October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on Blueberry Headband

Blueberry Headband succeeds because neither side of its ancestry completely dominates the finished cultivar. Blueberry contributes recognizable fruit, color potential, and physical depth, while the Headband influence adds vigor, potency, spice, and a livelier cerebral opening. The result is a high-THC hybrid that can move from upbeat and engaged to deeply relaxed without feeling one-dimensional.

Its horticultural performance is equally noteworthy. A 65-to-70-day indoor flowering period is manageable, yet outdoors the plant can grow to tree-like proportions and produce exceptionally heavy harvests. Combined with dense resinous flowers and a layered blueberry, spice, anise, pine, and fuel profile, those characteristics explain why Humboldt Seed Organization continued refining the genetics through multiple generations. For growers who have the room to control its vigor—and consumers who appreciate potent weed balancing fruit with old-school California pungency—Blueberry Headband remains one of the more distinctive hybrids to carry the Headband name.
